title: Improve rate limits + circuit breakers for diagnostics endpoints (incident-bot/Console)
author: Logan Wright
description: Context: During incidents we see a spike in diagnostics traffic driven by incident-bot v2 thread interactions + Console deep links. When upstream telemetry/config systems are degraded, retries/timeouts can turn into a burst that (a) increases tail latencies for responders and (b) adds load to already-sick dependencies. This PR adds explicit rate limits and circuit breakers to the diagnostics surface area (telemetry aggregation, config diff, and deploy metadata) to prevent self-inflicted load while still keeping the bot/Console useful in degraded conditions. Changes: (1) Introduce a shared "Diagnostics Guard" middleware that applies token-bucket limits (per service identity, per endpoint, and per tenant when available) with a small global safety cap; returns bounded responses with retry-after hints. (2) Add a dependency-aware circuit breaker around outbound calls to telemetry-query, config-service diff, and deploy-registry. Breaker opens on sustained p95 latency + elevated error rate; while open, endpoints return cached context (if present) plus deep links and a "degraded mode" banner instead of attempting live fanout. (3) Implement request coalescing + singleflight for identical diagnostic queries within a short window (reduces thundering herd from Slack retries). (4) Add load-shedding behavior: when diagnostics budget is exhausted, we skip expensive dimensions (tenant breakdown, high-cardinality labels) and fall back to region/service aggregates. (5) Metrics + alerts: export diagnostics_budget_dropped_requests_total, diagnostics_cb_state, diagnostics_upstream_latency_ms, and cache_hit_ratio. Wire to existing incident context dashboards to make the new behavior visible. (6) Configuration: add defaults tuned for #incidents usage, plus an allowlist override for SRE break-glass service identity (still audited; does not bypass the global cap). Testing: unit tests for token bucket math, breaker transitions, and degraded-mode payloads; integration tests with a fake upstream that delays/fails; manual validation by replaying a captured incident-bot interaction pattern from INT-3341. Rollout: behind a runtime flag DIAGNOSTICS_GUARD_ENABLED (default ON in staging, OFF in prod). After merge we will enable in prod for incident-bot service identity first, then Console server over 48h if no regression in diagnostics latency. Notes: This intentionally does not change Slack bot retry behavior (handled in incident-bot repo) but makes the backend resilient to those retries. Related: PR-29125 (tenant-aware metric query primitives), PR-29133 (audit events for bot access), ENG-5427 (telemetry caching/coalescing), ENG-5429 (bot load shedding).
commits: diagnostics: add DiagnosticsGuard middleware (token bucket + retry-after)
diagnostics: circuit breaker wrapper for telemetry/config/deploy dependencies
diagnostics: singleflight coalescing for identical query keys
metrics: export cb state + budget drops + cache hit ratio
tests: add unit + integration coverage for degraded-mode responses
config: add defaults + break-glass allowlist (global cap preserved)
snippet: Example behavior changes (degraded mode): when breaker is OPEN for telemetry-query, /diagnostics/telemetry_context responds with {"mode":"degraded","reason":"telemetry-query breaker open (p95>4s, err>20%)","data_source":"cache","links":["https://console.redwood.ai/obs/saturation?service=hosted-api&region=us-east-1&window=30m"],"missing":["tenant_breakdown","kv_cache_pressure_by_model"]} and includes header Retry-After: 30. Rate limiting returns HTTP 429 with a small JSON body: {"error":"diagnostics_budget_exceeded","scope":"service_identity:incident-bot","retry_after_s":15}.
review_conversation: Rafael Mendes (SRE): Can we guarantee we still return something useful when telemetry-query is timing out? Also please avoid hammering upstream with half-open probes during a real outage. Author: Degraded mode returns cached payload (last 5m) + deep links; half-open probe rate is capped at 1 probe/30s per dependency per region and respects the same global cap. Added metrics for probe attempts.

Miles Thornton (Incident automation): Slack interactions retry aggressively under load; does singleflight cover thread bursts? Author: yes—coalescing key is (endpoint, service, region, tenant?, time_window_bucket). Added a 2s window for in-flight dedupe and a 10s cache TTL for identical requests.

Aisha Bello (SLO/alerting): Please add an alert on sustained budget drops; otherwise we won’t notice the bot is starving responders. Author: added dashboard panel + alert suggestion (not paging) when dropped_requests_total increases > 50/min for 10m for incident-bot identity.

Marcus Lin (Security): Break-glass allowlist concerns—ensure it doesn’t bypass global caps and is audited. Author: break-glass only relaxes per-identity limits, not global cap; requests emit audit event diag.guard.break_glass_used with incident_id and requester identity (ties into PR-29133).

Caleb Johnson (Tracing/metrics): Be careful about new label cardinality (tenant_id). Author: tenant_id is only included in metrics when present AND sampled at 1%; otherwise we log it to structured logs with redaction. Updated metrics yaml accordingly.
outcome: Merged to main; enabled in staging by default. Follow-up: flip DIAGNOSTICS_GUARD_ENABLED for incident-bot prod identity after 24h soak; monitor diagnostics p95 latency + dropped requests and adjust per-endpoint budgets if needed.
release_notes: Reliability: Diagnostics endpoints now apply explicit rate limits and circuit breakers, returning cached context + deep links during upstream degradation to prevent self-inflicted load in incidents.
